title: On the Evolution of (Hateful) Memes by Means of Multimodal Contrastive Learning
measurement_description: The paper measures the capability of multimodal contrastive learning models to identify and track the evolution of hateful memes targeting specific groups. It specifically evaluates the automated detection of semantic regularities to find visual and textual influencers of identity-based hate, focusing heavily on antisemitism (e.g., the 'Happy Merchant' meme) and other memes targeting religious and ethnic minorities on 4chan's /pol/ board.
findings: The study found that the Jewish community is the most prevalent target of hateful memes on 4chan's /pol/ board. Using the CLIP framework, the authors successfully identified over 3.3K variants of the antisemitic 'Happy Merchant' meme. They observed that these antisemitic symbols are frequently fused with other cultural, political, and religious entities—including Muslims and Christians—to disseminate identity-based hate. The models effectively captured both visual and visual-linguistic semantic regularities to identify these hate-driven mutations.
